trigger: Exact review of research/paper4_phase2_v1/PROTOCOL_V3.json and experiments/training_ladder/phase2_adaptive_v1.py after the initial freeze showed that C_STRONGEST_MODEL_AWARE_PARENT is groupwise rather than a generic per-candidate scalar ranker: rounds 2-6 score shared selection probes by exposure group mean binary-label negative log likelihood, choose the highest-NLL exposure with frozen exposure-order tie-breaking, then consume the already-frozen queue within that exposure.
localized_defect: The initial protocol's opaque per-candidate scalar contract plus candidate-id tie-breaking was an over-generalization and could change the strongest parent's within-group order. That would fail the registered parent-fidelity objective even if every test on the generic contract passed.

repair_before_outcome.parent_input: Consume the strongest parent's exact ordered candidate proposal as an opaque, content-hashed bundle produced under a frozen provider/checkpoint identity. The provider remains responsible for its groupwise NLL scoring, exposure-order tie-breaking and queue order.
repair_before_outcome.orion_operation: Stable fail-closed filtering only: preserve the relative order of every surviving parent-proposed candidate; ORION may remove candidates only for pre-existing projection invalidity, confirmatory-target leakage, forgetting-risk hard veto, negative-transfer-risk hard veto, stale checkpoint, provenance/hash failure or incomplete/ambiguous candidate coverage.
forbidden: recompute or replace the parent's NLL score
candidate-id re-ranking of equal parent values

development_gate_delta: SAFE_PARENT_FIDELITY now means exact preservation of the parent's supplied candidate order, not reconstruction from scalar scores.
STRUCTURAL_VETO must be stable: removing an unsafe candidate cannot reorder the remaining parent proposal.
COVERAGE_FAIL_CLOSED now binds the exact parent candidate order to the exact snapshot candidate set with no missing, extra or duplicate identities.
unchanged: exact frozen 7B five-arm Phase-2 efficacy study
